audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 NCI income was $54m and distributions to NCI partners were $56m; net owner-earnings mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated depreciation, capital expenditures, and working-capital adjustments may be combined with net income attributable only to Quest, creating an inconsistent owner-earnings numerator before division by parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Income attributable to the minority interest in the Company's majority owned and controlled consolidated subsidiaries is recorded as net income attributable to noncontrolling interests in the consolidated statements of operations and the noncontrolling interest is reflected as a separate component of consolidated stockholders' equity in the consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that consolidated subsidiaries generate material minority economics, but the supplied record does not establish which adjustments in the $899m anchor were allocated to NCI. Using all depreciation could overstate owner earnings, while using all capital expenditures or working-capital investment could understate it; the net direction and materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct the 2025 attribution bridge by subsidiary or allocate every consolidated owner-earnings adjustment between Quest and NCI, then compare the resulting parent-attributable OE with $899m.

audit_findings.title: Modeled growth may require acquisition spending omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Business-acquisition cash outflows were $611m in 2023, $2,164m in 2024, and $101m in 2025; the recurring acquisition burden supporting modeled growth is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The model capitalizes 3%-5% growth while potentially excluding acquisition cash outlays from owner earnings and reinvestment requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: We endeavor to grow revenues each year by 1-2% through acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: Quest explicitly targets 1%-2% annual revenue growth through acquisitions, representing one-third to two-thirds of the modeled base-case growth rate. Historical acquisition spending is large relative to the $899m anchor, so omitting the capital required to obtain acquisition-driven growth is reasonably capable of materially overstating value. The error remains conditional because the record does not identify how much scenario growth was assumed to be organic.
audit_findings.action: Attribute each scenario's growth between organic and acquired sources and rerun the valuation with a recurring acquisition-cost or reinvestment charge for the acquired-growth portion.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI creates an unmodeled put claim and ownership transition
audit_findings.magnitude: $80m redeemable NCI, equal to 0.6% of the $13,257m base equity value or about $0.70 per diluted share; 2025 related NCI income was $7m and distributions were $10m
audit_findings.mechanism: A redemption payment reduces the equity bridge, while the resulting increase in Quest's ownership increases subsequent parent-attributable owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the sale of an 18.9 % noncontrolling interest in a subsidiary to UMass on July 1, 2015, the Company granted UMass the right to require the Company to purchase all of its interest in the subsidiary at fair value commencing July 1, 2020.
audit_findings.explanation: The put is a real claim, but deducting the entire current $80m carrying value without recognizing acquired minority earnings would change base value by only about $0.70 per share before the offsetting earnings benefit. That scale is insufficient to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm expected exercise timing and price, then document a consistent treatment pairing the redemption payment with the post-redemption increase in Quest-attributable OE.

audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes a pre-Corewell earnings anchor with a post-close balance-sheet date
audit_findings.magnitude: $38m cash consideration and $253m initial 49% NCI value; Corewell and Fresenius together contributed about 8 percentage points of the 12.0% first-half 2026 DIS volume growth, while Corewell's attributable OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes the post-close operation, while June 2026 cash and debt reflect the transaction; future consolidated results also require removal of Corewell's 49% economic share.
audit_findings.evidence: Equity ownership of the venture is shared 51 % by Quest and 49 % by Corewell Health and Quest will consolidate the business in its consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter-date mismatch. Excluding Quest's share of Corewell earnings and capital needs may understate value, while failing to remove the 49% minority share from consolidated adjustments may overstate it. The transaction and subsequent volume contribution are large enough to require an explicit perimeter treatment.
audit_findings.action: Build a post-close, Quest-attributable Corewell OE schedule including consideration, incremental earnings, maintenance capital, working capital, and 49% NCI; rerun on one consistently dated perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 liability was $100m, or 0.8% of $13,257m base equity and $0.87 per share; capitalizing the full $10m 2025 gain at the base OE multiple adds about $141m, making a conservative combined mechanical scale about $241m, 1.8% of base equity or $2.10 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid acquisition consideration is omitted from the equity bridge, and any retained $10m remeasurement gain inflates anchor OE and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.evidence: Of the aggregate $ 96 million contingent consideration obligation as of December 31, 2025, $ 45 million and $ 51 million were included in other liabilities and accounts payable and accrued expenses, respectively, in the Company's consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: Both mechanisms would overstate value if uncaptured. Nevertheless, even the conservative mechanical combination of the full June liability and the full pre-tax gain is about 1.8% of base equity value and does not alter the valuation conclusion. Whether the gain was actually retained in the $899m anchor remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $10m gain through normalized OE and confirm whether projected payment of the $100m liability is captured in cash flows; deduct or normalize the applicable amounts in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain a non-recurring payroll-tax windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $46m, equal to 5.1% of the $899m anchor; if fully retained, the computed base-value overstatement is about $646m or $5.63 per share, reducing base value to about $109.88 per share and buy-below to about $76.92
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-time credit increases 2025 earnings and operating cash flow and, if not normalized out, is capitalized through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company received $ 46 million from a payroll tax credit under the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act associated with the retention of employees.
audit_findings.explanation: The $46m non-recurring receipt and gain are demonstrated by the filings. Whether the valuation removed it is unresolved, but full retention would affect roughly 5% of the anchor and base valuation, making the issue material to the stated value and buy-below outputs even though it would not reverse the large price-to-value shortfall.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $46m credit through the exact OE bridge and rerun all scenarios after removing any amount retained in normalized owner earnings, preserving recurring restructuring, integration, and compliance costs.
